title: Recording and Replaying a Field Run: A Text Log That Carries Its Scenario, Survives a Cut Power Line, and Proves That Two Runs Were the Same

questions.question: How many digits does a double need to be given back exactly?
questions.explanation: Seventeen significant digits are enough to recover any double exactly, and sixteen are not always. The log writes 17.

questions.question: Written with 6 digits, a ten second run read back off by:
questions.explanation: Each value is rounded to six digits. That is small, and it is also enough to make two logs of the same run differ, or to hide a real difference.

questions.question: Two runs with different seeds first differed at:
questions.explanation: The noise is drawn from the seed from the first sample on. The same seed twice gave no difference at all.

questions.question: A log cut in the middle of a line read as:
options: 999 entries with the truncated flag set
An error at the last line
questions.explanation: The half written last line is dropped and flagged, and the rest is read. A wrong line in the middle is different: that stops the read at its line number.

questions.question: Why does the log carry its scenario?
options: So the record holds both the question and the answer
To make the file self checking
So the scenario file can be deleted
Because the format needs a header
questions.explanation: A log that holds only numbers cannot say what was asked of the robot. With the scenario in it, the run can be repeated from the log alone.

questions.question: How does the parser know the last line was cut?
options: It counts the entries against a header
The last time stamp is before the duration
The writer ends every line with a newline, and the text does not end in one
questions.explanation: A complete write always ends in a newline. If the text does not, the last line was never finished.
